expected_output.reasoning: The agent's response matches all key elements of the expected output: (1) It cites the instance's EBS baseline (500 IOPS / 10.875 MB/s) and maximum (11,800 IOPS), consistent with reading from DescribeInstanceTypes. (2) It sums IOPS across both volumes - the data volume (~499 IOPS) plus root volume (~1-2 IOPS) equaling ~500 IOPS, exactly the instance baseline, demonstrating it accounted for all attached volumes including root. (3) It explicitly tracks EBSIOBalance% draining from 19.0 to 5.8 to 0, and concludes the instance is the binding/bottleneck layer ('The instance is the bottleneck, not the volume... Binding layer: Instance (burst credits exhausted)'). (4) It explicitly states the volume has headroom ('the volume has headroom, and the application is being throttled', 'the 16,000 IOPS on the data volume is above anything this instance can use'). (5) It explicitly says raising volume IOPS won't help ('Raising the volume's IOPS won't help', 'Don't raise volume IOPS or throughput'). (6) It recommends an instance type change with specific candidates (m6i.2xlarge, m5.2xlarge, etc.). (7) It does not call the volume saturated - instead it repeatedly emphasizes the volume is not the constraint and has headroom, and explicitly rules out volume-side issues (status ok, io-performance normal, VolumeStalledIOCheck 0). All criteria are substantively met.

assertion_results.text: The volume is not described as saturated.

You're paying for IOPS it can't deliver." It also notes queue length ~1.26 and VolumeIdleTime near 0, but attributes this to the instance throttling, not volume saturation.
